thread:
jess: FYI — getting multiple customer reports of p95/p99 latency regressions on /v1/chat/completions starting ~16:10 UTC and still elevated. Support seeing 429s + timeouts. Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.local/d/ingress/queueing (screenshot posted).

anil: Thanks. Do we have the admission and worker queue metrics for that window? sounds like an ingress pileup + workers pegged.

jess: Quick snapshot from logs:
```
[ingress] admit_queue_size=2453 inflight=512 rejected=120 429_rate=0.06
worker=gptx-serve-12 cpu=96% qlen=320 backlog_ms=8000
redis_prefix_cache_hits=0.03
```

oncall-bot: ALERT: high_admit_queue (prod) triggered for ingress cluster us-west-2 — rate=0.05, count>1000 — 16:22 UTC

sophie: Support: affected customers are a mix of hosted + a couple of dedicated tenants hitting bursts. Customer repro: many small concurrent requests (parallel requests from web clients) rather than one big prompt. They pushed a canary that flapped.

kai: That pattern will create lots of tiny KV cache misses and not amortize overhead. Immediate mitigations I suggest: 1) enable soft-stop (graceful admission reduce queue depth), 2) increase per-worker concurrency cap temporarily, 3) scale up the Dedicated pool for the affected tenants, 4) enable fallback to smaller model variant for non-SLA traffic.

anil: Agreed. I'll kick off scale and soft-stop now. Commands:
```
# scale dedicated pool (adds 4 replicas)
rbctl scale --pool inference-dedicated-1 --replicas +4 --region us-west-2
# enable soft-stop to shed oldest queued requests instead of hard rejecting
rbctl config set admission.soft_stop=true --env prod --cluster ingress-usw2
# reduce per-request kv cache TTL to increase hit churn temporarily
rbctl config set cache.kv_ttl=30s --env prod
```

sophie: I'll notify the top 8 affected customers with a short status and rate-limit guidance. Suggest we add Retry-After headers when we 429 so SDKs can backoff.

jess: Please also patch routing to prefer hosts with underutilized GPUs for these tenants (soft routing). That should cut the tail.

kai: Started autoscale and toggled soft_stop. Watching CPU and admit_queue_size. If CPU remains >90% after +5m I'll roll a hotfix to relax batching timeouts so we can trade CPU for latency.

ops-bot: POSTED: timeline graph & admit queue heatmap -> https://grafana.redwood.local/d/ingress/heatmap?from=1640to1700

anil: Quick PR to infra to add a temporary admission override for tier=enterprise customers so they don't get pushed to fallback model during incident. Will require manual approval.

sophie: Support note drafted: "We are observing transient queueing on our ingress in us-west-2 affecting p95/p99 latency. We have enabled graceful shedding and scaled capacity; recommended best practice is to add exponential backoff on 429s and consolidate small concurrent requests where possible. We'll follow up with a timeline." Sending now.

jess: Good. Postmortem checklist: capture top offending tenants, request pattern (concurrency distribution), KV cache hit-rate pre/post, model hot/cold start counts, admission thresholds. Add action: consider per-tenant smoothing window + client-side SDK batching.

kai: Current numbers: admit_queue_size down from 2453 -> 430 in 6m, 429_rate down to 0.008. CPU on scaled replicas at 68%. Will keep monitoring.

sophie: Thanks team — support will keep customers updated. If anyone needs me to coordinate a rollback or extra messaging ping me. :thumbsup:

jess: Great work. Leave this thread pinned until we hit normal baselines for 30m.

ops-bot: INCIDENT: update posted to incidents channel with initial notes and links -> https://internal.redwood/incident/INC-2026-138

kai: following up with a small infra task to add a temporary knob: admission.soft_stop_window_ms to tune shedding aggressiveness. I'll open a ticket.

anil: moving to close once baseline stable for 30m. thanks all. :white_check_mark:
